reading: Four 3x3 red shapes scattered on a large grid are gathered into a 7x7 grid: each shape keeps its pattern and goes to the quadrant (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) matching its relative position, with a 1-cell empty gap row/column between them.

slots.pieces: the four 8-connected objects, each with a 3x3 bounding box (copied box by box)
slots.layout: 2x2 arrangement ordered by the pieces' relative row and column positions
slots.spacing: one empty row and column between pieces; output size 7x7

why: each output 3x3 corner block equals the bounding box of the input object lying in that relative quadrant

reading: Grey shapes below the blue shape turn red when some rotation/reflection of the shape can be pushed up into one of the blue shape's downward-open holes and fill that hole completely (any remainder hanging below the blue shape without touching blue); other grey shapes stay grey.
verb: recolour shapes that plug a hole

new_rows.name: plug
new_rows.datalog:
g(O, Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), cell(Y, X, 5).
lt(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, 1).
lb(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, 1).
hole(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), lt(T), lb(B), Y >= T, Y <= B.
up(Y, X) :- hole(Y, X), cell(Y2, X, 1), Y2 < Y.
lf(Y, X) :- hole(Y, X), cell(Y, X2, 1), X2 < X.
rt(Y, X) :- hole(Y, X), cell(Y, X2, 1), X2 > X.
cav(Y, X) :- up(Y, X), lf(Y, X), rt(Y, X).
reach(Y, X, Y, X) :- cav(Y, X).
reach(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- reach(Y, X, Y1, X1), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y1 + DY, X2 = X1 + DX, cav(Y2, X2).
ky(Y, X, min(Y2)) :- reach(Y, X, Y2, X2).
kx(Y, X, min(X2)) :- ky(Y, X, KY), reach(Y, X, KY, X2).
ck(Y, X, KY, KX) :- ky(Y, X, KY), kx(Y, X, KX).
rot(O, 0, Y, X) :- g(O, Y, X).
rot(O, 1, Y, NX) :- g(O, Y, X), NX = 0 - X.
rot(O, 2, NY, X) :- g(O, Y, X), NY = 0 - Y.
rot(O, 3, NY, NX) :- g(O, Y, X), NY = 0 - Y, NX = 0 - X.
rot(O, 4, X, Y) :- g(O, Y, X).
rot(O, 5, X, NY) :- g(O, Y, X), NY = 0 - Y.
rot(O, 6, NX, Y) :- g(O, Y, X), NX = 0 - X.
rot(O, 7, NX, NY) :- g(O, Y, X), NX = 0 - X, NY = 0 - Y.
place(O, T, KY, KX, SY, SX) :- rot(O, T, A, B), ck(CY, CX, KY, KX), SY = CY - A, SX = CX - B.
pc(O, T, KY, KX, SY, SX, Y, X) :- place(O, T, KY, KX, SY, SX), rot(O, T, A, B), Y = SY + A, X = SX + B.
bad(O, T, KY, KX, SY, SX) :- pc(O, T, KY, KX, SY, SX, Y, X), cell(Y, X, 1).
bad(O, T, KY, KX, SY, SX) :- pc(O, T, KY, KX, SY, SX, Y, X), lb(B), Y <= B, !ck(Y, X, KY, KX).
miss(O, T, KY, KX, SY, SX) :- place(O, T, KY, KX, SY, SX), ck(CY, CX, KY, KX), !pc(O, T, KY, KX, SY, SX, CY, CX).
fits(O) :- place(O, T, KY, KX, SY, SX), !bad(O, T, KY, KX, SY, SX), !miss(O, T, KY, KX, SY, SX).
plug(Y, X) :- fits(O), g(O, Y, X).

why: every cell of a grey (5) shape that can fill a hole of the blue (1) shape becomes red (2); the blue shape and the non-fitting grey shapes are unchanged

reading: Each single coloured pixel slides in a straight (orthogonal or diagonal) line toward the nearest grey 2x2 block and stops at the first cell touching it (8-adjacency); the grey blocks stay.

new_rows.name: single
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
single(Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), osize(O, N), N = 1.

why: every 1-cell object keeps its colour and ends 8-adjacent to a grey (5) block, reached by a straight or diagonal path; markers are not usable as subject because some pixels touch each other

reading: Two pixels (upper and lower) each draw a pattern in their own colour: the upper colour draws the top half (rows 0-4): full row 0, full row through the pixel, and both side columns; the lower colour draws the bottom half (rows 5-9): full row through the pixel, full last row, and both side columns.

slots.upper colour: colour of the pixel in the top half; paints top border row, its own row, side columns of rows 0-4
slots.lower colour: colour of the pixel in the bottom half; paints its own row, bottom border row, side columns of rows 5-9
slots.split: grid cut into top and bottom halves

why: every non-empty output cell lies on a border row/column of its half or on the row of that half's pixel, coloured by that pixel

reading: A 3x3 multicoloured block shoots rays: each of its 8 outer cells extends in its own colour away from the centre cell (edges straight, corners diagonally) to the grid border; the centre cell does not extend.
why: every outer block cell continues as a straight line in the direction from the block centre through that cell until the border, in that cell's colour

reading: The grid is 3x3 panels split by separator lines; the top-left panel holds a template shape. In every panel, each template position that is still background is filled with the separator colour; existing cells stay.

new_rows.name: spot
new_rows.datalog:
sepc(C) :- px(5, 0, C).
srow(R) :- px(R, 0, C), sepc(C).
pstart(S) :- px(S, 0, C), S = 0.
pstart(S) :- srow(R), S = R + 1.
tmpl(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y < 5, X < 5.
spot(Y2, X2) :- tmpl(Y, X), pstart(A), pstart(B), Y2 = Y + A, X2 = X + B, px(Y2, X2, 0).

why: every background cell at a template offset inside any panel becomes the separator colour (which differs per pair, so the colour is the separator's, not a training constant); nothing else changes
invariants: cells already coloured in other panels

reading: Each 3-cell L shape (on background 7) gets a copy of itself shifted one diagonal step: grey-5 L's are copied in colour 4 toward the missing corner of their 2x2 box; red-2 L's are copied in colour 3 away from their missing corner. Copies paint only background cells; where a 3 and a 4 copy overlap, 3 wins.

slots.subject: each L-tromino object (colour 5 or 2)
slots.offset: one diagonal step: toward the empty corner of its 2x2 box for 5, away from it for 2

why: every new cell belongs to the shifted copy of an adjacent L in its mapped colour

reading: A 2x2 block contains some red (2) cells; the block is swept diagonally toward each red cell's corner direction until the grid edge, painting the swept band (and the block itself) in the block's other colour.

slots.subject: the 2x2 block
slots.directions: for each 2-cell, the diagonal pointing from the block through that corner

why: every output cell of that colour is a cell of the block translated k diagonal steps (k >= 0) in one of the marked directions

reading: The 3x3 grid is scaled up by 2: each grey (5) cell becomes the 2x2 tile [1 2 / 2 1] and each 0 cell becomes a 2x2 of 0.
why: output block (r,c) is the fixed tile when input cell (r,c) is 5, else empty

reading: The top panel is a key: three 3x3 colour blocks with one marker pixel under each (row 4), mapping marker colour -> block colour. The output is the bottom panel (below the full separator row), where every marker pixel becomes a 3x3 block of its mapped colour centred on it.

slots.key: marker colour in the row under each key block -> that block's colour
slots.canvas: the panel below the separator row (13 rows), background 7
slots.anchors: each marker pixel in that panel
slots.unit: 3x3 solid block centred on the marker, colour from the key

why: every 3x3 block in the output is centred on a marker of the bottom panel and coloured by the key; all other cells are 7
invariants: marker positions (relative to the bottom panel)
